summary: The mass comparison and its moment consequence are valid. Both occupation-class transformations have the stated multiplicity ratios, injective maps on classes for each fixed m, and correctly directed comparisons of complete height tails. The estimates for the low-one classes, including the B=2 case and both alternatives defining h, imply the claimed exponential bound. The clipping estimate covers the complementary regimes, including R>=k in (2). The accepted three-site theorem applies with B_i=B, unchanged ambient halfspaces, and normalizer Z_3; the fourth power of the mass fraction gives exactly (3). Increasing the fourth-site cost, including to a noninteger value, preserves the unchanged three-site portion and decreases the full normalizer. Zero budget, small dimension, beta=0, cap equalities, and singleton height intervals are covered. No mathematical error or gap was found.
